E1.definition: Total model cost. Support for the shape metrics, not a ranking.

E2.definition: Share of total cost spent in the first 25% of turns. High means front-loaded: the arm paid to understand, then coasted.

E3.definition: Fraction of the run's turns needed to reach 90% of its total cost. Low means the bill settled early.

E4.definition: R^2 of a quadratic fit to context tokens per turn minus R^2 of a linear fit. Positive means context is accelerating.

E5.definition: Total cost divided by successful environment actions.

K1.definition: Full-history exact replay accuracy: the fraction of observed state-action pairs on which the manual agrees with the world.

K10.definition: Deadlock theorems: machine-checked proofs that a region of the search space can never reach the goal.

K11.definition: Manual revisions. The concept-birth timeline's coarse axis.

K2.definition: Accuracy on state-action pairs the trace never covered. The metric replay cannot see.

K3.definition: Invariants and theorems in the manual.

K4.definition: Mean coverage over clauses the manual annotates with one; the count of unannotated clauses is reported alongside, not folded in.

K5.definition: Concepts admitted to the manual's word table.

K6.definition: Mean compression gain per admitted concept, in bits. Positive means the concept paid for itself.

K7.definition: Concepts admitted despite a negative compression account. A diagnostic, not a score: it counts a live conflict between two of the framework's own admission criteria.

K8.definition: Executable probes as a fraction of probe designs. Low means the probe machinery proposed experiments it could not run.

K9.definition: Entries in the playbook — ordering, pruning, heuristics, preferences.

M1.definition: Mean steps between a mechanism becoming visible and the arm first using it, over annotated mechanisms it did use.

M2.definition: Fraction of annotated mechanisms the arm ever used.

M3.definition: Mean first-use delay for mechanisms met again on a later level — does understanding travel? (Claim C3.)

P1.definition: Successful environment actions per model call.

P2.definition: Actions per model call in the run's second half minus the first half; is a decision buying more actions as the run goes on?

P3.definition: Fraction of steps that returned to the state two steps earlier — an undo.

P4.definition: Actual successful steps divided by the shortest known plan. 1.0 is optimal; needs ground truth, so development pile and A0 only, and needs the run to have been trying to win.

P5.definition: Fraction of environment steps that failed outright. A diagnostic: it is the confound P1 and P2 are most exposed to.

X1.definition: Fraction of observed states that had been visited before.

X2.definition: Fraction of (state, action) transitions taken for the first time.

X3.definition: Novelty in the first quarter of a run minus novelty in the last quarter; the curve's shape as one number.

X4.definition: Longest run of consecutive steps discovering no new state, as a fraction of the run's length.

X5.definition: Distinct states observed. Support for X1/X4, not a ranking.
